name: Agniveer Army GD
fullName: Indian Army Agniveer (General Duty) – Online Common Entrance Examination
nameHi: भारतीय सेना अग्निवीर (जनरल ड्यूटी) सामान्य प्रवेश परीक्षा
approxCandidates: Several lakh registrations per cycle (approx.; the Army does not publish exact figures)
eligibility: Class 10 with 45% aggregate and 33% in each subject. Age 17½–21 per the scheme; reports say the upper limit was raised to 22 for the 2026 registration cycle, so check the current notification

notification.summary: Registration for recruiting year 2027 ran from 13 February to about 10 April 2026, and the online CEE was held from 1 to 16 June 2026. ARO-wise CEE results were published on 12 July 2026, and recruitment rallies (physical tests and medicals) followed from late July 2026. The next cycle's registration is expected around February–March 2027 on joinindianarmy.nic.in.

pattern.stage: Phase I – Online Common Entrance Examination (CEE), Agniveer GD
pattern.notes: The section split (15/15/15/5) and the marking of +2 / −0.5 follow the widely reported GD pattern since negative marking was introduced in 2023. Secondary sources disagree on the marking, so check it against the current Army notification. The pass mark has been reported as 35 out of 100. Phase II is the recruitment rally (physical fitness and measurement tests, adaptability test, documents and medical). The bank holds 60 items: GK 18, Science 18, Maths 18, Reasoning 6.

trendAnalysis.summary: The paper is at Class 10 level and mostly easy to moderate. General Science (basic Physics, Chemistry and Biology facts and units) and General Knowledge (Indian history, geography, polity, defence and static GK) are the most scoring areas. Mathematics covers arithmetic, mensuration and simple algebra or geometry, and it was reported as the toughest section in the June 2026 CEE. Reasoning is short: series, coding, analogy and directions. Because of negative marking, accuracy matters more than attempting everything, and difficulty has been stable since the CEE format began in 2022–23.

resources.notes: The Army does not publish CEE question papers or answer keys. joinindianarmy.nic.in carries the notification, syllabus, practice or mock-test links and ARO-wise results, and papers circulating online are memory-based.

pyqBlueprint.method: The Army does not publish CEE question papers. Patterns come from memory-based 'questions asked' reconstructions and candidate-feedback analyses of the Agniveer GD CEE in 2024 (April–May), 2025 (30 June–3 July) and 2026 (June), together with the published syllabus and the 15/15/15/5 GD pattern reported by Aglasem, Arihant and Business Standard. WebSearch found no full question-level analysis, so item types are confirmed from these summaries and the writer's own knowledge of the Class-10-level paper. Patterns are described in our own words.

archetypes.pattern: Freedom fighters and leaders: titles, slogans and associates ('Iron Man', 'Netaji', 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan').
Monuments, builders and places of historic events (Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, 1857 revolt).
Indian geography superlatives and origins (largest state, longest river, coastline, glaciers, deserts).
World geography basics (largest ocean, continent).
Constitution basics: dates, number of duties, articles for rights, age limits, appointments, nominated members.
Basic economy facts: currency issue, RBI, GST introduction.
Sports terms and team sizes (hockey, chess terms).
National awards and what they honour (Bharat Ratna, Khel Ratna).
Gallantry awards and military days (Param Vir Chakra, Ashoka Chakra, Army Day).
Army commands and training establishments with their headquarters.
National symbols, and books with their authors.
Countries with their capitals and currencies.
SI units and approximate physical constants (force, resistance, g, c, horsepower).
Measuring instruments and devices with the energy conversion they perform.
Light: mirrors and lenses, their uses and properties.
One-step numericals on speed, acceleration and work.
Chemical formulas and common names of compounds (common salt, washing soda, caustic soda).
Acids, bases and pH; indicators and everyday acids.
Elements and gases: atomic number, liquid metal, abundant/light gases, hardest substance.
Cell organelles and organs and their functions.
Vitamins and minerals: deficiency diseases.
Human body systems: heart, blood components, body temperature.
Prime numbers and divisibility tests.
LCM and HCF of 2–3 numbers.
BODMAS simplification and fractions.
Square roots, squares and decimals.
Percentage of a number, reverse percentage and election-margin problems.
Profit/loss and finding cost price from selling price and gain/loss %.
Dividing a quantity in a given ratio.
Average of consecutive numbers or multiples.
Simple interest: amount, rate or time.
Compound interest for 2 years, compounded annually.
Time and work: joint work and men–days proportion.
Speed unit conversion (km/h ↔ m/s) and distance problems.
2D figures: perimeter and area of squares, rectangles and circles.
3D figures: volume and surface area of cubes and cuboids.
Linear equations in one variable.
Angles: triangle angle sum, complementary and supplementary angles.
Number series (×2, squares, differences).
Letter series with increasing or constant gaps.
Letter-shift coding or letter-position sum coding.
Word analogy (function, worker–workplace).
Odd one out among words or numbers.
Direction sense: turns and distance from the starting point.
Simple blood relation chain (grandparent/grandchild, nephew).

questions.question: Find the next letter in the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
questions.explanation: Positions 2, 5, 10, 17 increase by 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9: 17 + 9 = 26 = Z.

relevance.note: Letter series with gaps 3,5,7,9 - typical Agniveer letter-series

questions.question: In a certain code, ARMY is written as ZINB. How will NAVY be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter in the alphabet (position p → 27 − p): A→Z, R→I, M→N, Y→B. So N→M, A→Z, V→E, Y→B, giving MZEB.

relevance.note: Opposite-letter (A<->Z) coding with army word; options differ by one letter as in CEE

questions.question: Pen : Writer :: Scalpel : ?
questions.explanation: A pen is the tool of a writer, and a scalpel is the tool of a surgeon. A butcher uses a cleaver, not a scalpel.

relevance.note: Tool:user analogy, exactly the CEE function analogy type

questions.question: From his camp, a soldier walks 5 km towards the North, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 9 km. How far and in which direction is he now from the camp?
questions.explanation: Taking the camp as (0, 0): north 5 → (0, 5); right (east) 3 → (3, 5); right again (south) 9 → (3, −4). Distance = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km, to the South-East.

relevance.note: Classic turns-and-distance with 3-4-5 triple; direction-swapped distractors

questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, Raman said, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the girl in the photograph related to Raman?
questions.explanation: Raman's grandfather's only son is Raman's father. The daughter of Raman's father is Raman's sister.

relevance.note: Photograph-pointing blood relation, exactly CEE style; Cousin/Niece distractors
